acceptance.output_evidence:
RECORDED FOR L9, NO VERDICT.

1. ONE IDENTITY OR TWO FOR FWD-11, AND THE COST. The SAME DynamoDB principal COULD carry advisor-shaped claims on one login (for FWD-1/2/5's firm-scoped testing) and be added to the /opal/irpt/opal-principal-roster SSM parameter for a SEPARATE login exercising FWD-11's OPAL_GLOBAL class -- _scope/global.py's FirmBinding is re-derived per SELECTED firm and per request, so no single concurrent session serves both classes, but nothing prevents one identity from qualifying for both classes across two logins. THE REAL COST NAMED HERE, MEASURED LIVE THIS RUN: the SSM parameter /opal/irpt/opal-principal-roster does not exist at all (aws ssm get-parameter -> ParameterNotFound) -- so the limiting factor for FWD-11 is not 'one identity vs two', it is that NO identity, bounded or not, can resolve OPAL_GLOBAL today until that parameter is created, which is a separate infrastructure act (its own sign-off) this cell's <paths> do not cover (infra/aws/lambda/investor-reporting/_scope/global.py:64-65 @391e4ad948869b8972bf6d96d5cc54392b351d5e).

2. WHETHER THE IDENTITY PLANE HAS DRIFTED FROM THE PRD'S B1/B2. Measured this run against the REAL Enforcer wired exactly as production wires it (infra/aws/lambda/investor-reporting/directory/entry.py:151-157 @391e4ad948, which never passes id_projection): a real FIRM_ADVISOR request against 49financial's live ownership map is refused UNPROJECTED_GRANT before the served/empty-grant branch is reached (43 of 43 grants unmatched), and this is not particular to the advisor or firm chosen -- 0 of 22,646 ownership-map account grants across all 179 advisors join the live directory even with the SAME projection function (_ids.projection_for) applied by hand outside the live wiring, and 0 of 13 live entry/handler/dispatch modules in this project ever pass id_projection to Enforcer/Entry (infra/aws/lambda/investor-reporting/_ids/ids.py:69-74, /_scope/resolve.py:247-276, /_authz/enforce.py:210-230, all @391e4ad948). So YES, the identity plane has drifted from what B1/B2 (and this project's own PRD framing that the test principal 'is therefore round 5's highest-value cell...THIS IS WHAT MAKES FWD-1/FWD-2/FWD-5/FWD-11 GRADABLE AT ALL', CTO round-4 analysis s.6(a) @561d6e1cc9) assumes: the tenant-scoping MECHANISM (FirmBinding, guard(), the six-guard covers()) is sound and IB-rt-2/IB-rtb-1 measured it correctly end-to-end against FIXTURE data whose ownership and directory ids were already in the SAME (opaque) space by construction -- but no cell before this one ran the real Enforcer against REAL, LIVE 49financial ownership-map data end-to-end, and doing so surfaces a code-wiring gap (id_projection never passed) that a bounded test principal cannot route around, because the refusal fires on the OWNERSHIP GRANT'S OWN SHAPE, not on the identity minting it.

3. WHAT REMAINS UNEXERCISABLE EVEN WITH THE PRINCIPAL, NAMED. (i) FWD-1/FWD-2/FWD-5's SERVED (200) path against live 49financial data -- blocked by the UNPROJECTED_GRANT wiring gap above, independent of the principal; the REFUSAL mechanism and the fixture-grounded mechanism batteries remain exercisable and valid. (ii) FWD-11 in its entirety -- blocked by the absent SSM roster parameter, independent of the principal. (iii) The two POST routes (submit analysis, submit export) stay excluded per bound 1/2 (no live vendor call, no notification) regardless of any identity. (iv) The download route's real-object grounding (row IRPT_BCKEND-W1-S18, carried from round 2/IB-rtb-1) -- the four synthetic export PDFs the estate ever produced are permanently gone, so even a working principal cannot exercise a real download artifact today, only the reauthorization mechanism against a labelled fixture. (v) cottonwood's own version of FWD-1's terminated-client behaviour -- its live directory carries termination.indicator=UNKNOWN for 260 of 260 entries, never ACTIVE or TERMINATED (row IRPT_BCKEND-W1-S24), so no principal at cottonwood could exercise the gap FWD-1's CONSTRAINT names until its producer populates the field.
